clue.text: Old woman caught a convict in Spain

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for one's mother, an old woman
an old lag is a slang term for a habitual convict

explanation.surface: An elderly lady apprehends a prisoner while abroad in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' just links the old woman to her convict; the pieces sit side by side. The definition is loose: a place in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaga is a port city on the Costa del Sol in southern Spain.

clue.text: Old railway worker is a businessman

parts.note: ex- means former, so old
a porter carries luggage at a railway station

explanation.surface: A former station porter has gone into trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader who sells goods overseas is a kind of businessman.

clue.text: Gone for a-on the river near Derby

parts.note: 'gone for a Burton' is British slang for killed or ruined, so the phrase completes with this word
upon is a formal way of saying on
the Trent is a major river of the English Midlands

explanation.surface: Someone lost or killed on a river near the city of Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash stands for the missing word in the British idiom 'gone for a Burton'. Burton upon Trent is a brewing town in Staffordshire close to Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: The brewing town lies about a dozen miles south-west of the city of Derby in the English Midlands.

clue.text: To a rich eccentric it was an old vehicle

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, telling us the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A wealthy oddball owned an antique carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' looks like a description of a rich person but signals rearranging TO A RICH; 'it was' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled horse-drawn war cart of antiquity is an ancient conveyance.

clue.text: Sharp prod?

parts.note: a prod with a sharp tip could be called this, but the phrase also means a cutting nudge to someone's memory

explanation.surface: A jab with something keen-edged.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbed hint that jogs someone's memory, like a sharp prod to recall a duty.

clue.text: Obscure humour of a stupid person

parts.note: dim means faint or obscure
wit is clever humour

explanation.surface: Unclear jokes told by a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dim-witted fool is a slow, unintelligent person.

clue.text: Dean spilt port

indicators.note: spilt suggests letters scattered like a knocked-over drink, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cathedral dean knocks over his glass of port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink spilt by the Dean, but it is a harbour town, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a seaport city in Yemen at the mouth of the Red Sea.

clue.text: Unknown race of cats

definitions.note: plural in the clue, while the answer names a breed of them

parts.note: man can mean mankind, the human race
x is the algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A mystery breed of cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link. The cats from the Isle of Man are famous for having no tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The tailless breed from the Isle of Man is a well-known kind of feline.

clue.text: One does not like to say it

definitions.text: One does not like to say it

parts.words: One does not like to say it
parts.note: read as an exclamation uttered by someone who dislikes something, rather than a word one avoids

explanation.surface: A word people avoid saying.
explanation.definitionFit: This interjection expresses disgust, the noise made by someone who dislikes a thing.

clue.text: Does not start the film again in Spain

indicators.note: a word that does not start has lost its first letter

parts.note: a movie is a film
do, short for ditto, means the same again

explanation.surface: A remake of a film fails to get going while on location in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: DO is the abbreviation of ditto, used in lists for 'the same again'. The definition is loose: a place in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Oviedo is the capital city of Asturias in northern Spain.

clue.text: Most unusual modern exit

explanation.surface: A very strange contemporary doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyphenated it means avant-garde or extremely unconventional; as two words it is the door you leave by.

clue.text: Reviving Frenchman at the branch

parts.note: Rene is a common French man's name
a wing is a branch of an organisation or building

explanation.surface: A Frenchman restores himself at an office branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Renewing something restores it, bringing it back to life.

clue.text: Certainly not gainfully employed

parts.note: suggests someone without paid work, but the sense is someone doing nothing useful

explanation.surface: Someone definitely not in paid work.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle or futile activity yields no gain, so one is not usefully occupied.

clue.text: It has to be crazy to stop up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a dam stops a river's flow

explanation.surface: Someone must be mad to stay up late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It has to be' and 'to' are links; 'stop up' looks like a phrasal verb but splits into a synonym and the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad is a common synonym for insane or wildly foolish.

clue.text: Others pray following the treatment

indicators.note: following means the second piece comes after the first
others suggests different versions of the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some people pray after medical treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Others' turns PRAY into RAPY, which follows THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is curative treatment of illness or disorder.

clue.text: Weed, he has nothing inside

indicators.note: inside means the second piece is placed within the first

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A man has weeded his empty garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link. 'Weed' is the verb, to clear weeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear unwanted plants from soil you work it with a garden tool, so the verb fits.

clue.text: Newly-wed accepts award for a print

indicators.note: accepts means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a bride is newly wed
the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A bride receives an award for a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link. A bromide is a photographic print on silver bromide paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A photograph printed on paper coated with silver bromide is called by this name.

clue.text: Periodical storehouse

explanation.surface: A storeroom full of journals.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular glossy publication, and also an arsenal where ammunition is stored.

clue.text: Suffer from ground shifting round the point

indicators.note: round means the scrambled letters enclose the next piece
shifting means the letters move into a new order

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone suffers from subsidence as the ground moves near a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' makes UNDRGO from GROUND, which goes 'round' E. 'from' and 'the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo hardship is to experience or endure it.

clue.text: Does it never lose its attraction?

definitions.text: Does it never lose its attraction?

parts.words: Does it never lose its attraction
parts.note: sounds like an enduring charm, but attraction here is physical pull on iron

explanation.surface: A question about something whose appeal never fades.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnetised piece of steel keeps its pull on iron indefinitely.

clue.text: I find this very painful in India

parts.note: 'my!' is the exclamation of someone who finds something surprising
sore means aching or very painful

explanation.surface: Someone in India complains of great pain.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a place in India. Mysore, now Mysuru, is a city in Karnataka.
explanation.definitionFit: Mysore is a historic city and former princely state in southern India.

clue.text: Join forces

parts.note: looks like an idiom for cooperating, but means signing up to the armed services

explanation.surface: Combine efforts together.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign up for military service is to become a member of the armed services.

clue.text: Keep book behind piano

indicators.note: behind means the first piece named follows the second

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
to book a seat is to reserve it

explanation.surface: Keep the book behind the piano.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve something is to maintain or save it.

clue.text: It is the standard measure

explanation.surface: A statement about a standard measuring device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It is the' is a link. A rule is both a principle or norm and a ruler for measuring length.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule is a norm or principle to follow, and a straight ruler for gauging length.

clue.text: Open end of the tube

parts.note: suggests a terminus of the London Underground, but it is the spout on a hose or pipe

explanation.surface: A terminus on London's Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: The spout at the tip of a hose or pipe through which fluid issues.

clue.text: Old coin for apprentice included inside

indicators.note: included means one piece is put within another

parts.note: L is a learner, as on British learner plates
in means inside

explanation.surface: An apprentice is given an old coin while indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: A FLORIN was a British two-shilling coin, worth ten pence after decimalisation.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a pre-decimal British silver piece worth two shillings.

clue.text: It is said to give encouragement to a horse

definitions.text: It is said to give encouragement to a horse

parts.words: It is said to give encouragement to a horse
parts.note: a word spoken to a horse to urge it on or turn it

explanation.surface: A word spoken to urge on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: This interjection is the command a rider or carter calls to make a horse go faster.

clue.text: Refusal to be quiet with food

parts.note: no is a refusal
sh is the instruction to be quiet

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to stay silent over a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'with' are links. NOSH is British slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal word for grub or a meal.
